po_a2.title: Exact-fit admission
po_a2.policy_quote: An exact amount fit is admitted.

steps.title: Lookup and accounting
steps.reason: The proof relates Ledger.find to the independent Spec.lookup and obtains the stored totals.

steps.title: Input terms
steps.reason: Key and amount range over Lynx.Term. Case splits eliminate representations excluded by eligibility.

steps.title: Eligibility and validity
steps.reason: Unfolding the precondition supplies valid entries, matching counters and capacity bounds.

steps.title: Independent lookup
steps.reason: The compatibility lemma establishes equality of the two separately implemented lookups.

steps.title: Required transition
steps.reason: The proof unfolds the actual request, expected output and independent reference.

steps.title: Remaining arithmetic
steps.reason: The remaining arithmetic goals follow from the capacity inequalities already obtained.

po_a2.omits: This admission law does not establish processor behavior, journal durability or every later transition.

po_exposure_retain.title: Pending void retention
po_exposure_retain.policy_quote: An approved authorization continues consuming capacity while voiding, until a trusted terminal confirmation is journaled.

steps.title: Valid starting state
steps.reason: The proof obtains Spec.valid? from the actual requires predicate.

steps.title: Remembered entry
steps.reason: The lookup-shape lemma separates absence from a stored entry. The required lookup excludes absence.

steps.title: Protected statuses
steps.reason: The precondition restricts the remembered entry to sent, unknown, authorized or voiding.

steps.title: Release evidence
steps.reason: The proof excludes the two events that count as terminal release evidence for this identity.

steps.title: Retention lemma
steps.reason: The final lemma covers the remaining transition cases and requires the entry to remain exposed.

po_exposure_retain.omits: A locally consistent released state can still violate retention. Applicability to remote authorizations additionally depends on the coupled environment model.

po_b1_timeout.title: Timeout validity
po_b1_timeout.policy_quote: A timeout or restart never releases capacity.

steps.title: State structure
steps.reason: Accounting, shape and update lemmas support preservation of the valid-state predicate.

steps.title: Changing sent to unknown
steps.reason: The helper goal establishes validity after the status update.

steps.title: Transition cases
steps.reason: The proof considers encoded keys and lookup outcomes for the timeout transition.

po_b1_timeout.omits: Validity alone does not require retention: a released entry with correctly reduced counters can be valid.

po_b1_void.title: Void validity
po_b1_void.policy_quote: An approved authorization continues consuming capacity while voiding, until a trusted terminal confirmation is journaled.
po_b1_void.omits: This law demands validity. Compare its result on a coherent early release with po_exposure_retain, which demands continued exposure.
